newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says savings won't rein in 96 budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: Buba says savings won't rein in 96 budget deficit.

text.p: Even rigourous savings efforts launched this year will likely not be sufficient to prevent Germany's deficit from expanding in 1996, the Bundesbank said in its Decemember report, released on Tuesday.

The public sector deficit, which in 1995 was at 3.5 percent and clearly above the three percent target level put down in the Maastricht Treaty, is likely to be even further away from the goal this year, the Bundesbank said.
It quoted the Bonn finance ministry's prediction that the deficit ratio to the gross domestic product will likely be around 3.75 percent, but declined to give its own prediction.
The government debt, according to Bonn's predictions, will be near the Maastricht Treaty's 60 percent reference value, or just slightly above it, the Bundesbank said.
It also said that German tax revenue will likely be one percent lower this year than last year. This matches government forecasts.
